summary: Master route optimization and distribution network design with Excel Solver, KPI dashboards, and practical planning exercises. Enrol now.
lede: Planning delivery routes and distribution networks helps logistics teams balance transport costs, vehicle capacity, and delivery windows. Designed for transport planners, distribution managers, logistics analysts, and fleet coordinators, the course covers measuring transport performance, optimizing stop sequences under capacity and time-window constraints, and comparing route and network scenarios using Excel Solver, delivery-zone mapping, KPI dashboards, and carrier scorecards.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who manage delivery routes, fleet utilization, distribution coverage, and transport performance. It is especially relevant if you need to turn operational data into route plans, network options, and management reporting that can stand up to service, budget, and compliance pressure. Transport Planner responsible for daily route sequencing and delivery schedules. Distribution Manager overseeing service coverage, fleet use, and cost control. Logistics Analyst measuring OTIF, route cost, and lane performance. Fleet Coordinator managing vehicles, driver allocation, and dispatch readiness. Route Planning Specialist testing delivery scenarios and stop optimization. Supply Chain Operations Manager balancing transport cost and service targets. Transport Controller monitoring execution variance and exception handling. Logistics Network Analyst mapping customer clusters and delivery zones. Carrier Manager allocating lanes and reviewing service performance. Operations Excellence Lead reporting transport improvement plans to leadership.
prerequisites: Participants should bring a laptop with Microsoft Excel installed and enough spreadsheet familiarity to sort, filter, calculate, and build simple models. If available, bring sample stop lists, delivery schedules, vehicle capacity data, or route performance reports for use in exercises. A basic understanding of transport operations is expected, while advanced optimization knowledge is not required.
